name: Extreme heat
summary: BoM severe heatwave warning for north Queensland; SAWS heat warnings in South Africa; no deadly top-tier event
state: The Bureau of Meteorology's warning issued at 12:18pm on 14 Nov says severe heatwave conditions will continue over the Peninsula and spread to the North Tropical Coast and Tablelands, with maximums in the high 30s to low 40s°C, before easing over the Gulf Country early in the week of 16 Nov (WillyWeather, citing BoM). The South African Weather Service warned on 11 Nov of heat reaching dangerous levels, with over 40°C forecast at Upington and veld fire risk in Gauteng, the Northern Cape and the Free State (EWN). Regional warnings meet the Watch line; no deadly heatwave under top-tier warnings across a large population was found as of 15 Nov.
for_you: Heat mainly affects older people, young children, outdoor workers and those with heart or lung conditions. Travellers to northern Australia or South Africa can follow the Bureau of Meteorology, the South African Weather Service and FCDO travel advice.
rubric_hit: Watch: heatwave warnings across a major region (BoM severe heatwave, north Queensland; SAWS heat warnings); no deadly top-tier event

sources.title: WillyWeather — Heatwave warning for Peninsula, Gulf Country and North Tropical Coast (BoM)

why: Heat is the deadliest weather hazard globally, straining power grids, crops and health systems.
drivers: Heat domes, climate warming, season, humidity, urban heat islands.

rubric.alert: Deadly heatwave with top-tier official warnings across a large population.
rubric.watch: Heatwave warnings across a major region, or national temperature records.
rubric.normal: No major heatwaves affecting large populations.
